newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 12.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 12.6 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading averaged 12.6 percent of its average daily trading volume of 510.6 million shares, or 64.2 million shares, for the week of March 3-7.
Of the 64.2 million shares traded during the week, buy programs accounted for a daily average of 28.5 million shares and sell programs an average of 35.7 million shares

In all markets, program trading averaged 92.2 million shares in the week. NYSE accounted for 69.6 percent, non- U.S. markets 14.4 percent, and domestic markets, including Nasdaq, American Stock Exchange and regional markets, 16 percent.
The five member firms reporting the most program activity were BNP Securities, NatWest, Morgan Stanley, Salomon Bros and Interactive Brokers.
All five executed all or most of their program activity for cutomers, as agents or facilitator, NYSE said.
Program trading includes a wide range of portfolio-trading strategies involving the purchase or sale of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a total value of $1.0 millon or more.
